data.title: Azelaic acid 20% cream
data.summary: VII Anti-acne — Others · Naturally occurring saturated dicarboxylic acid (from Malassezia furfur)
data.body:
_Topicals · VII Anti-acne — Others_

**Class:** Naturally occurring saturated dicarboxylic acid (from Malassezia furfur)

## Mechanism of action
- Antibacterial against C. acnes and staphylococci; normalises keratinisation (comedolytic)
- Competitive inhibitor of tyrosinase and toxic to abnormal (hyperactive) melanocytes → treats hyperpigmentation without affecting normal skin
- Anti-inflammatory and anti-oxidant (reduces reactive oxygen species, KLK5/cathelicidin in rosacea)

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Acne vulgaris (mild–moderate), especially with PIH
- Papulopustular rosacea (15% gel — approved)
- Melasma, PIH, lentigo maligna (historic)
- Safe option in pregnancy

## Dose & formulations
- Twice daily; results by 4–8 weeks (acne), 2–3 months (melasma)

## Adverse effects
- Transient burning, stinging, itching (common at start)
- Rarely hypopigmentation in dark skin (watch)

## Contraindications
- Hypersensitivity (propylene glycol in gel)

## Pregnancy & lactation
Safe in pregnancy and breastfeeding (old FDA category B).

## Viva points
- Tyrosinase inhibitor that acts only on hyperactive melanocytes
- Acne + rosacea + melasma in one drug
- Pregnancy-safe acne treatment

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.57 (azelaic acid); Khopkar ch.26 (Demelanizing agents). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
